stage: P0-1 Stage A pre-registration (frozen before any Stage A label or prediction exists)
question: On independently human-confirmed fingerspelling spans, can the letters be read, and does a hand-RGB recognizer add information over the existing keypoint recognizer? Diagnostic only; reported separately from automatic localization (Stage B) and fusion (Stage C).

keypoint_baseline.name: OpenFS recognizer (CVPR 2026, AIRC-KETI)
keypoint_baseline.architecture: EncoderDecoderTransformer, input_dim 42 (21 hand points x 2D), d_model 256, 8 heads, 3 layers, ff 2048
keypoint_baseline.preprocessing: MediaPipe Holistic 0.10.9 (model_complexity 1, full frame, single signer, no YOLO crop); a hand is kept on a frame only if its wrist is above its elbow; per-hand upstream normalize(.5); compact per-hand frame indices
keypoint_baseline.decoding: greedy, max 32 tokens, open vocabulary over '$abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz .&\'@'; no lexicon, no language model
keypoint_baseline.abstain: fewer than 8 hand observations in the span -> abstain (insufficient_hand_observations); an empty decoded string also counts as abstain
keypoint_baseline.runner: asl-translator/experiments/p0-2026-10-27/specialist.py model path, unchanged, with the span taken from the human label instead of fixed windows
keypoint_baseline.platform: Apple M3 Pro, Python 3.11.7 x86_64 (Rosetta), torch 2.2.2 CPU, mediapipe 0.10.9, numpy 1.26.4, 2 threads; known platform/encode sensitivity (boss strings reproduce 10/18)
keypoint_baseline.note: never to be described as hand-RGB fusion

rgb_primary.name: HandReader_RGB (ai-forever/HandReader, arXiv 2505.10267)
rgb_primary.licence: code: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE sha256 c71d239d...). checkpoint: trained on ChicagoFSWild+; checkpoint and data use remain subject to the relevant dataset/checkpoint terms, not necessarily covered by the code licence
rgb_primary.variant: RGB: TSM ResNet-34 (unidirectional shift) + 2-layer BiGRU head (1024), CTC, configs/rgb_chicago.yaml (sha256 3ccc1c1b...)
rgb_primary.checkpoint: HandReader_ChicagoFSWild+.zip (sha256 f66a5c77...) -> chicago+/rgb/best.pt sha256 fa92e90db23a467c59d47e718f07233b94d73c1bff8dfdf3a2248ed4f3c9ad0a (strict load: 241 tensors, 0 missing, 0 unexpected)
rgb_primary.input: per-frame RGB hand crops; eval transform Normalize(ImageNet mean/std) then Resize(224,224), ToTensorV2; frames concatenated with per-clip lengths; no temporal resampling. Upstream ships no crop code (training crops came from the Shi et al. 2019 localizer); Stage A uses the shared MediaPipe crop pipeline below

decoding.primary: CTC beam search, beam size 5, no language model, no lexicon (upstream beam_decode, scorer None, so lm_beta/ins_gamma are inactive)
decoding.secondary: upstream greedy_decode, diagnostic only; never used for a metric or gate
decoding.why: the upstream greedy decoder can collapse a legitimate repeated letter: after 2+ emitted characters it skips a letter equal to the previous emitted letter, even across a blank
decoding.not_claimed: beam decoding is not claimed to be more accurate on our data
decoding.freeze_statement: This decoder choice was frozen before any Stage A evaluation output was produced and therefore was not selected based on benchmark accuracy.

rgb_primary.runtime: CPU, Python 3.11.7 x86_64 (Rosetta), torch 2.0.1, torchvision 0.15.2; runtime patches P1 (no ImageNet download at construction) and P2 (Tensor.cuda no-op on CPU), no model logic change; see results/p0_1_handreader_rgb_feasibility.json
rgb_primary.status: feasibility PASSED 2026-10-29 on a synthetic input; NOT run on any Stage A item
risks: crop-source shift (MediaPipe crops vs the training localizer)
ChicagoFSWild+ domain vs How2Sign studio video

rgb_fallback.name: MiCT-RANet (fmahoudeau/MiCT-RANet-ASL-FingerSpelling), ChicagoFSWild+ weights
rgb_fallback.input: full RGB frames (224/256p) plus Farneback optical flow; attention finds the hand, no crop
rgb_fallback.checkpoint: released (Proton Drive): MiCT-RANet34.pth (V1) and MiCT-RANet18 ChicagoFS large (V2)
rgb_fallback.licence: NOT stated on the repo page: research use must be confirmed before use
rgb_fallback.decoding: CTC beam search, beam 5, no language model
rgb_fallback.use_if: HandReader cannot be installed or run on CPU, or its checkpoint cannot be verified

spans.positives: human-confirmed span(s) from blind Step 1 (fingerspelling_present = yes, letters given, letters_confidence high or medium); both recognizers get exactly the same span
spans.negatives: items labelled fingerspelling_present = no; both recognizers get the frozen probe window from the input-side screen (no human span exists)
spans.uncertain: excluded from primary metrics; counted and reported
spans.localization: none: Stage A never uses a detector for the temporal span

pipeline.timing: ffprobe best_effort_timestamp_time per decoded frame of the frozen clip; frame_index, clip_time_s (PTS) and source_time_s (How2Sign START + PTS) logged separately; no resampling
pipeline.span_frames: frames with start <= clip PTS < end
pipeline.landmarks: one MediaPipe Holistic 0.10.9 pass (complexity 1) over the span frames, shared by both recognizers
pipeline.hand_side: human-labelled signing hand when left/right; otherwise the hand with more valid raised frames in the span (tie: right); same hand for both recognizers
pipeline.keypoint_input: OpenFS path unchanged (both raised hands, as upstream), frames with detected landmarks
pipeline.rgb_crop: selected hand; square box centred on the landmark bbox, side 1.6 x max(w,h), min 64 px; centred median over 5 detected frames; gaps <= 4 frames linearly interpolated (status interpolated); longer gaps -> hand_missing, frame dropped from RGB input; box shifted (not shrunk) inside the frame; resized to the recognizer's input size
pipeline.missing_hand: logged per frame; if fewer than 8 usable frames remain, the recognizer abstains
pipeline.naming: files and metadata carry blind_id only; no reference text, name or clip title

label_schema.blind_id: FSA-### only; no clip ID, case ID or source name is shown
label_schema.video_file: blind-named copy of the frozen clip; clip time = file time
label_schema.span_no: 1, 2, ... one row per fingerspelling span; one row with span_no 1 if none
label_schema.span_start_s / span_end_s: clip seconds (file time), span level only; per-letter times are NOT collected
label_schema.letters: letters seen, a-z, as signed (no correction to an English word); '?' for an unreadable letter; blank if not readable
label_schema.visibility_issue: none | motion_blur | out_of_frame | low_resolution | lighting | other

label_procedure: Step 1 blind: the reviewer sees only the blind-named clip. Step 2 (reference-conditioned) is not part of Stage A scoring.

metrics.normalisation: lowercase; keep a-z only (spaces, punctuation, digits removed) for both label and output; a human '?' letter is kept as a wildcard that matches any single letter

primary.CER: sum of Levenshtein edits / sum of human letters over positive spans; an abstain is scored as the empty string (all deletions)
primary.word_exact: fraction of positive spans whose normalised output equals the normalised human letters

secondary.abstain_rate: abstains / spans (positives and negatives reported separately)
secondary.fpr_negatives: fraction of negative items where the recognizer emits >= 2 letters on the probe window
secondary.coverage: spans with a non-abstain output / spans
secondary.per_letter_confusion: substitution pairs from the Levenshtein alignment
secondary.runtime_per_span_s: median and max wall time per span

metrics.paired: per-span CER difference (RGB - keypoint); wins / losses / ties (tie if |delta| < 0.05); 95 % bootstrap CI of the mean per-span difference, clustered by source video, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261029
subgroups: Uni-Sign already-correct controls (human letters appear as a token in the Uni-Sign A_official output, derived after labelling)
metrics.control_subgroup_rule: The 36-item selection does NOT use Uni-Sign output. After blind human labels return, an 'already-correct Uni-Sign control' subgroup may be defined by comparing the blinded human-confirmed letters against the previously saved Uni-Sign A_official output. The subgroup is analysis-only after labelling and cannot affect which 36 items were selected.
metrics.not_used: model self-confidence is never used as correctness or for abstain decisions

gates.G0_validity: at least 12 positive spans with letters (confidence high/medium) and at least 8 negatives; otherwise no verdict (insufficient labels)

rgb_adds_value_all_of.G1_cer: RGB corpus CER <= keypoint CER - 0.10 (absolute) AND the upper bound of the 95 % cluster-bootstrap CI of the mean per-span CER difference (RGB - keypoint) < 0
rgb_adds_value_all_of.G2_word: RGB whole-word exact accuracy >= keypoint whole-word exact accuracy
rgb_adds_value_all_of.G3_false_positives: RGB FPR on negatives <= keypoint FPR + 0.10
rgb_adds_value_all_of.G4_breadth: after removing the 2 spans with the largest RGB gain, RGB corpus CER is still < keypoint CER, AND per-span wins >= 1.5 x losses

gates.readable_at_known_spans: the better recognizer reaches CER <= 0.35 AND whole-word exact >= 0.30 on positives; otherwise Stage A says: improve the recognizer first, postpone Stage B and fusion

outcomes.NO_RGB_GAIN: G0 passes and any of G1-G4 fails

gates.fixed_before_results: thresholds are fixed here, before any Stage A label or prediction exists, and must not change after results are seen

expansion_rule: if Step-1 labels leave G0 unmet, label further items in this fixed order, in batches of 8: remaining eligible clips by descending screen score (eligible_screen_table), each batch taking up to 6 by score and 2 by salted hash; stop as soon as G0 is met or the 61-clip pool is exhausted. Beyond that, a How2Sign test raw-video pool (outside the 128) needs new keypoints and a separate approval. Items added this way are flagged expansion = true.
